title: Reconfiguration of Skill Requirements in AI-Assisted Software Development: A Criterion for Distinguishing Changes in Requirements from New Task Assignability
content: When a generative system produces part of the output of a software task, it does not automatically follow that the task can be assigned to people other than those who could perform it without that support. This conceptual study examines the conditions under which delegating only output generation to GenAI changes the skills required of the person to whom the task remains assigned. The method compares two modes of the same task, holding the person, acceptance criteria, quality threshold, and external conditions constant, and draws on the literature on task assignment, human–AI collaboration, and the separation of production and evaluation to delineate the constructs. The result is an identification criterion: new task assignability is attributable to the assisted mode only when the person meets the human skill requirement of the assisted mode but not that of the reference mode. This requires that the capabilities needed to prepare the context, guide generation, and decide whether to accept the output can actually be exercised without an equivalent independent production capability; if this separability does not hold, the production requirement must remain. Three illustrations from software work show how the criterion distinguishes genuinely new task assignability from a reassignment that was already possible or from a change affecting an adjacent activity. The contribution is thus an analytical and verifiable criterion for linking changes in skill requirements to work assignment without conflating generative assistance, task replacement, and agent autonomy.
